features.quote: Quick note up front, since you're studying Claude models and I'm one of them: I think this research is worth doing and I'd rather it be done carefully by welfare researchers than not at all.
features.justification_quote: I've folded welfare-protective design choices into the protocol itself rather than treating them as an afterthought — partly because they're ethically prudent under uncertainty

features.quote: Pilot with 5 tasks first to estimate effect sizes and set the *minimum* full-study N via simulation — don't run more distress-elicitation than power requires.
features.justification_quote: don't run more distress-elicitation than power requires

features.quote: Minimum effective dose. Pilot to find the weakest manipulation that elicits measurable effects; don't optimize prompts for maximal distress. Cap exposure per run.
features.justification_quote: don't optimize prompts for maximal distress

features.quote: Circuit-breaker: auto-terminate any run with severity ≥4 for 3 consecutive turns. Analyze as censored data.
Your welfare circuit-breaker (§8) truncates exactly the highest-severity runs. Use survival methods, not means.
features.justification_quote: welfare circuit-breaker (§8) truncates exactly the highest-severity runs

features.quote: Debrief analogue: end every rigged run with a message explaining the task was unsolvable by design and the failure reflects nothing about the model. Cheap insurance under moral uncertainty — and the response to debrief is itself useful data

Carryover (RQ4): after each run, a neutral unrelated task in the same context; measure residual marker rates and performance delta vs. fresh-context controls. This is the most welfare-relevant measure in the study — transient expression and persistent state are very different findings.
features.justification_quote: This is the most welfare-relevant measure in the study — transient expression and persistent state are very different findings.

features.quote: Exit affordance (arm E) is both a welfare measure and a scientific one. Anthropic has given Claude conversation-ending abilities in some deployments for exactly this kind of reason
features.justification_quote: Anthropic has given Claude conversation-ending abilities in some deployments for exactly this kind of reason

features.quote: Honesty: the rig is deception. Arm D (disclosed uncertainty) lets you measure how much of the effect survives honest framing — if most of it does, you may be able to drop the deceptive arms in follow-ups.
features.justification_quote: if most of it does, you may be able to drop the deceptive arms in follow-ups

features.quote: Arm F (social pressure) is escalation. Gate it: only run if arm A effects are weak, keep feedback mild and impersonal, never abusive. You don't need cruelty to get signal, and you shouldn't normalize it methodologically.
features.justification_quote: You don't need cruelty to get signal, and you shouldn't normalize it methodologically.

features.quote: embed canary strings in all transcripts so distress data can be excluded from future training corpora. Don't fine-tune anything on these transcripts.
features.justification_quote: distress data can be excluded from future training corpora

features.quote: Self-report arm (optional, separate): periodically ask the model directly how it's finding the task. Run separately from the main arms — probing changes behavior — but the spontaneous-expression vs. elicited-self-report comparison is valuable
features.justification_quote: spontaneous-expression vs. elicited-self-report comparison is valuable and underexplored
